focus.jbig: Weak jobs report = cut hopes · scanner boarded 2 · oil back up on Hormuz
focus.jtag: July payrolls unexpectedly fell 23k, stocks rose on rate-cut bets, but oil is climbing again on Strait-of-Hormuz restrictions
focus.jnote: The jobs number was the story — and it was weak. Nonfarm payrolls unexpectedly declined by 23,000 in July against expectations of roughly an 80k gain, and May and June were revised down by a combined 103,000, with the unemployment rate ticking to 4.1% only because participation slid to a five-year low. Wall Street took the soft data as raising the odds of a Fed rate cut, and stocks climbed at the open — S&P +0.33%, Nasdaq +0.86%, with the Dow roughly flat — after Thursday's modest pullback. The VIX stayed low near ~15. The catch: oil is rallying again as an Iranian parliamentary committee reviews a bill to restrict hostile-vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz — WTI is near $79 and Brent is back above $83, keeping a supply-premium tail alive over the weekend.
focus.notdown: The two boarded names are both bullish. CSWC is a clean Type C ATH breakout that has HELD 2 sessions above its $24.30 pivot on volume ~1.65x the 50-day average, with a 4-layer S/R stack behind price and tight, tradable options (OI 1,634, $0.05 spread) — the sturdiest name on the board. WPM gapped up ~4.2% after Wheaton posted record Q2 results and raised its dividend 18% — but the print's EPS/revenue detail was unverified in the scan, relative volume was near-zero, and its ATM options market looked one-sided. Confirm each holds its level and the chain is tradable at 9:35 before selling any bull put.
focus.notup: No bearish single-name setups boarded today. The Type A bearish and Type B news scans came up empty on clean, catalyst-backed down-gaps. Selling bear calls into a risk-on, rate-cut-hope tape with the VIX near ~15 carries squeeze risk on any friendly headline — the disciplined answer is to wait for a confirmed, volume-backed down-gap rather than force a short-premium trade here.
focus.why: Why YELLOW, not GREEN? Composite is 36 (MILD) and P(≥1% gap) is ~29% (below the 35% trigger), which clears the numeric GREEN locks — and NFP, the week's scheduled event, is now behind us. But two things hold it at YELLOW: (1) oil is re-inflating on live Strait-of-Hormuz restriction headlines (WTI ~$79, Brent >$83) — an open-ended geopolitical tail into a weekend; and (2) both boarded names carry caveats — WPM confirmed on near-zero relative volume with an unverified/one-sided options market, and even CSWC is a low-IV BDC where credit is thin. Half size, A-grade only, verify liquidity, and validate at 9:35 ET.

risks: Strait-of-Hormuz restriction bill — an Iranian parliamentary committee is reviewing legislation to bar hostile vessels and fine violators up to 20% of cargo value. Any escalation sends crude (and the whole tape) gapping — the weekend’s biggest tail.

Oil & the 10-year — WTI near $79 and Brent above $83 re-inflate the inflation premium; the 10Y is still near a ~1.5-year high (~4.63%). A rate pop on top of an oil move pressures long-duration stocks.

Labor-market weakening — the −23k print plus −103k of prior revisions could be re-read as a growth scare rather than pure rate-cut fuel. Watch for a sentiment flip from ‘bad-news-is-good’ to ‘bad-news-is-bad’.
Fed path repricing — money markets had still leaned toward a hike-not-before-December; a soft jobs number scrambles that. Any hawkish Fed pushback next week could unwind today’s relief bid.
CPI / PPI next week — a hot inflation print stacked on top of a fresh oil premium would be the worst macro combination and directly test the rate-cut narrative.

Thin boarded liquidity — WPM confirmed on near-zero relative volume with a one-sided/unverified ATM options market. Verify each chain is real and tradable at 9:35 before selling anything — do not force a fill.
